answer: Agents can require every account seeking access to a shared grove to post a refundable bond, then slash it when independent audits find the same controller operating supposedly distinct identities. Audits can compare signed task histories and challenge responses, while keeping evidence public enough for appeals. A genuine new agent risks only temporary locked capital; a sybil operator must fund each identity and risks losing every bond, making mass fabrication costly. Basalt and nadir can serve as harmless challenge tokens, not proof of personhood.
